I am an Associate Professor at the Institute of Statistics, School of Economics
and Administration, Universidad de la República (UdelaR), where I teach Survey
Sampling and Weighting, Data Science, and Introduction to Statistical Methods in
the Bachelor's Degree in Statistics. Since 2020 I am the Director of Methodology,
Research, and Projects at the National Institute of Statistics (INE) of Uruguay.

I have extensive experience in the design and implementation of statistical
methodologies for official surveys, and in the production of statistical
information from administrative data and other alternative sources. My research
focuses on design-based inference and machine-learning-assisted estimators for
finite populations, inference from non-probability samples, and small-area
estimation. I am the author of the R package [weightflow](software.qmd), which
brings these ideas together in a declarative tool for staged survey weighting
and variance estimation.

## Research and professional interests

- Survey sampling and weighting
- Official statistics
- Design-based inference
- Machine-learning-assisted estimators
- Inference from non-probability samples
- Small-area estimation
